title: Strain Mapping Using HR-EBSD Versus 4D STEM on a Direct Electron Detector
content: Strain in materials is important for the performance of electronic devices by affecting the mobility of charge carriers [1]. This can hinder performance and be used to tune electronic properties. Strain can also be used to stabilize certain phases and is critical in the development of certain high-performance alloys [2]. At the nanoscale, 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) and scanning precession electron diffraction (SPED) are commonly used to measure strain with spatial accuracies of 1-10 nm and precision of +/- 0.05-0.1% [3].
